Hello from my home town in New Orleans... 
Castnet is indeed ONE of the best seafood houses in New Orleans, having been going there pretty much since birth with my family, but to say it is the "best seafood market"?.... ummmm NO!!! 
Come on Mark... I have come across a few of your videos pertaining to my city and even though I love your videos and appreciate your enthusiasm, your titles could be misleading. If this title were "ONE of the Best Seafood Houses..." then I would not have a problem, but you can't title a video with a false narrative. You have done that a few times in New Orleans so I had to point that out to you as a local man born and raised... but now I am skeptical to know if you indeed do this on all your videos and destinations.?!

comments.author: @JamVee
comments.text:
Some years back (about 1984), I worked on a Project at the Kennecott Refinery in Magna Ut. One of the largest parts of our work, was the electronic guidance systems that moved the Copper product through the refining process. The Contractor that did that work was from New Orleans (pronounced "Nawlins") Louisiana. At the project's completion they flew a whole plane-lode of "CRAWFISH BOIL" TO Salt Lake City and we feasted most of a Saturday Morning on that amazing spread. Everyone was invited, from the craftsmen to management an the client too. They rented a U-Haul truck to haul it all to the jobsite.
If you've never had a Louisiana Crawfish Boil, you haven't lived. Fresh and steaming in 10 gallon pots. Loaded with Crawfish Shrimp, Corn on the cob, chunks of fresh garden veggies, a ton of amazing herbs and spices and, fresh fingerling potatoes. Pick-nick tables covered with newspapers and the spread just dumped out onto the tables in piles. We did it in the parking lot, so we could have beer, which they supplied too. It went on for hours, until you couldn't eat anymore.
That occasion, will live forever in my memory.
